full_judgment:
11. First opposite party who was Thirty Three Defendant in suit sought setting aside the decree passed ex parte on presentation of a petition under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code. The said petition has been numbered as Miscellaneous Case No. 41 of 2001. In Miscellaneous Case plaintiffs-petitioners were First-Third Opposite Parties and other defendants of suit were Fourth-Fortieth Opposite Parties. First opposite party on 28- 11-2001 laid two petitions; one for dispensation with service of notices upon Fourth-Fortieth-Defendants-Opposite Parties and another for staying the operation of decree recorded in Title Suit No. 8 of 2002. 

 15. Rule 13 enshrines that in any case in which a decree is passed ex parte against a defendant, he may apply to the Court by which the decree was passed for an order to set it aside and if he satisfies the Court that the summons was not duly served, or that he was prevented by any sufficient cause from appearing when the suit was called on for hearing, the Court shall make an order setting aside the decree as against him. 

 23. This Rule arising out of Civil Revision Petition under section 115 of the Code is devoid of any substance and same stands discharged. Order dated 28-11-2001 recorded by learned Assistant Judge, Amtali, Barguna in Miscellaneous Case No. 41 of 2001 springing out of Title Suit No. 8 of 2000 stands good and maintained. 

 25. Miscellaneous Case No. 41 of 2001 laid under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure shall proceed in accordance with law.
